Select the MTD Contour from Completed Waterfall Trials

Source: R/waterfall_select_mtd.R
waterfall_select_mtd.Rd

Choose the maximum tolerated dose at every dose level of drug A for each of a set of completed trials of the waterfall design, from the final patient and DLT counts and the combinations excluded during the trial.

Usage

waterfall_select_mtd(n_pts, n_tox, eliminated, target)

Arguments

n_pts

Integer matrix giving the number of patients treated at each combination of one trial, with one row per dose level of drug A and one column per dose level of drug B, or an integer array with dimensions trial by level of drug A by level of drug B for several trials, as returned by waterfall_simulate.

n_tox

Integer matrix or array of the same shape as n_pts, giving the number of DLTs observed.

eliminated

Logical matrix or array of the same shape as n_pts: whether the combination is excluded from the selection, as returned by waterfall_simulate.

target

Numeric scalar. Target DLT probability.

Value

A data frame with one row per trial and dose level of drug A and columns

trial

Trial index.

dose_a

Dose level of drug A.

dose_b

Dose level of drug B of the MTD at that level of drug A, or NA when none is selected.

Details

The selection follows BOIN::get.oc.comb() with mtd.contour = TRUE. The estimates (y + 0.05) / (n + 0.1), set to 1.1 at the excluded combinations, are smoothed by bivariate isotonic regression with weights n + 0.1, so that they increase along every row and column, and 1e-5 times the sum of the two dose levels is added. From the highest level of drug A to the lowest, the treated combination of the row that is not excluded and whose estimate is closest to target is selected. A row whose first combination is excluded, or without a treated combination that is not excluded, has no MTD. When the MTD of a row is not at a higher level of drug B than the MTD of the row above it, it is moved to the level of drug B of that MTD, so that the contour does not turn back; the combination it is moved to need not have been treated.

The isotonic regression is Iso::biviso(), the routine the reference implementation calls.

BOIN::select.mtd.comb() with mtd.contour = TRUE ends with a different rule (a row takes the last level of drug B when the row above has its MTD there, and has no MTD when both are there); the operating characteristics of BOIN::get.oc.comb() come from the rule described here.

References

Zhang, L. and Yuan, Y. (2016). A Practical Bayesian Design to Identify the Maximum Tolerated Dose Contour for Drug Combination Trials. Statistics in Medicine, 35(27), 4924-4936.

See also

waterfall_simulate, sim_waterfall

Examples

n_pts <- matrix(c(3, 3, 9,
                  6, 9, 3), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
n_tox <- matrix(c(0, 0, 3,
                  1, 3, 2), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
eliminated <- matrix(FALSE, nrow = 2, ncol = 3)
eliminated[2, 3] <- TRUE

waterfall_select_mtd(n_pts, n_tox, eliminated, target = 0.30)
#>   trial dose_a dose_b
#> 1     1      1      3
#> 2     1      2      2
